title: POC Weekly Sync - Model selection & pinning
next_steps: Maya to send updated benchmark spreadsheet with per-model latency/cost by 2026-03-12
Carlos to run the requested 1k query KV-cache stress test and share logs by 2026-03-15
Customer to confirm production traffic patterns and SLOs by next sync (2026-03-17)
action_items: Carlos: run KV cache stress test (due 2026-03-15)
Samir: provide 1-week traffic distrib and top-10 prompt set (due 2026-03-17)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining. well kick off, i think we have about 40 minutes. quick roll call?
[00:06] Samir: yep Samir here, hi.
[00:09] Laura: Laura on my side.
[00:11] Jared: Jared here.
[00:13] Carlos: Carlos from Redwood, e--- SE.
[00:16] Maya: cool. agenda today is quick results review from last week's runs, model selection tradeoffs, pinning strategy and the rollback/fallback plan if we see regressions.
[01:05] Samir: sounds good. first question, uh, overall the latency numbers — we saw the hosted run was around 220ms median but tail was spiky, can you unpack that?
[01:22] Carlos: yeah so the 220ms is for the rtx-optimized variant we ran in dedicated-like env; the spiky tails were largely due to KV cache misses and one node hitting a GC pause in our harness, not production infra. also batch sizing — some of the auto-batching pushed a couple of larger micro-batches.
[01:40] Maya: to add, the catalog comparison spreadsheet we sent shows 95th at ~520ms for the Flex-v1 config, whereas the Quant-P2 (int8) profile has 95th ~430ms but slightly higher hallucination in the eval set.
[02:05] Laura: by hallucination do you mean factuality drop or token-level coherence?
[02:12] Carlos: mostly factuality on product attribute extraction prompts; coherence was comparable. we flagged a couple of prompts where the quantized runs dropped the brand-name entity recognition.
[02:34] Samir: ok that matches what we saw. for Capstone, precision on SKU attributes is more important than shaving 10% latency. so leaning towards higher-quality model, maybe use quantized as fallback.
[02:49] Maya: exactly, that's why we're proposing pinning to the higher-fidelity variant (Catalog-Large-v2) for read path, and use the Quant-P2 as fallback when Dedicated capacity constrained.
[03:05] Jared: what does pinning mean operationally here? like can we pin per-route? per-customer?
[03:12] Carlos: yep, per-route and per-deployment. you can pin model version at route-level in the config; we also support weight-based rollout (canary/beta) and automatic fallback to a compatible variant if primary isn't available.
[03:27] Laura: is fallback automatic or do we need to configure thresholds?
[03:31] Carlos: you configure policies. e.g., if median latency > 600ms or error rate > 2% we failover to fallback variant. we can set per-route SLOs.
[03:45] Samir: are the fallbacks compatible in output schema? i.e., the embeddings vector dim, tokens?
[03:50] Carlos: must be compatible yes — same tokenizer and output dims. if not compatible we do a degrade path where we call a lightweight transformer to reformat, but that's extra latency and complexity, so we prefer compatible variants.
[04:12] Maya: quick note — security mention from last meeting: you asked for SAML SSO + audit logs export. we've uploaded the security pack and SOC2 attestation to the shared drive. 
[04:26] Laura: saw that, thanks. one ask: can you show us audit log format?
[04:31] Maya: yeah i'll attach a sample csv in the follow-up.
[04:35] Jared: on dedicated sizing — the burst capacity model we discussed, how does that affect committed cost?
[04:40] Carlos: burst lets you absorb spikes without full reserved pools; you pay a small premium on top of reserved. the optimizer also suggests optimal batch sizes to reduce token cost. we're modeling a sweet spot for you at 8-12 token-batch windows for typical prompts.
[05:05] Samir: that 8-12 number, is that per GPU or per worker?
[05:08] Carlos: per worker. it uses continuous batching across concurrent requests to fill micro-batches.
[05:14] Samir: ok. next, the benchmark spreadsheet showed inference cost per 1k requests — was that with or without KV cache?
[05:21] Maya: spreadsheet has both columns; base cost without caching, and effective cost with prefix/KV caching applied. for your traffic pattern caching reduces token compute by ~22% on our sample.
[05:36] Laura: good. can we lock model pinning to routes for specific tenants? we might want different pinning for checkout vs search.
[05:45] Carlos: yes it's route-level. you can also set traffic rules so that checkout is strict (Catalog-Large-v2 pinned) while search uses Catalog-Medium with quantization.
[05:58] Samir: about rollbacks — if we push a canary and see a quality regression, how quick is rollback?
[06:04] Carlos: rollback is immediate in control plane; we can automate detection via eval prompts and metrics and rollback on alert. the propagation to workers is usually sub-30s for our control plane and config sync.
[06:18] Maya: we recommend a canary window of 1k requests or 15 minutes for heavy traffic routes to catch safety regressions.
[06:28] Jared: what about comparison vs OpenAI API — you mentioned cost advantage — can you summarize?
[06:35] Maya: rough numbers from spreadsheet: per-1k token cost effective is about 40-60% lower for our Dedicated quantized path vs a comparable hosted endpoint from major providers. caveat is you trade some ops overhead and integration.
[06:55] Laura: we also have compliance concerns: can you confirm data residency options? we need EU region for some data.
[07:02] Carlos: yes we can pin region, Private deployment supports VPC options and on-prem if needed. audit logs and KMS integration supported.
[07:12] Samir: okay digging into the concrete test results: last run we saw a 3% drop in exact-match for attribute extraction on Quant-P2 vs Catalog-Large-v2. can you re-run with the latest tokenization tweak?
[07:28] Carlos: sure — we made a tokenizer update last week that slightly improved entity boundaries. i'll re-run the 2k prompt eval across 3 seeds and share diffs.
[07:38] Maya: noted as Carlos action item.
[07:41] Samir: also we want to test fallback under capacity pressure. can you simulate a full Dedicated pool outage and verify automatic fallback to hosted?
[07:51] Carlos: yes we can run chaos testing in the staging harness — simulate node loss and ensure routing to hosted fallback. we'll record latency and any degradation.
[08:03] Laura: one more on dev experience — how easy to change pinning via API? we want programmatic toggles in our deploy toolchain.
[08:12] Carlos: full REST and SDK support; feature-flaggable via our rollout APIs. we can give you a sample script.
[08:20] Samir: can we see an example of a policy config? like JSON?
[08:24] Maya: we'll push a sample policy in the follow-up.
[08:27] [12:00] (discussion continues; timestamps jump as speakers interleave)
[12:05] Samir: on the eval set, which metrics are you surfacing? we need precision/recall, token-level perplexity, and a domain-specific business metric.
[12:14] Carlos: we provide BLEU-ish metrics, exact-match, F1 for entities, and you can plug in custom metrics. the Optimize console can alert on regression for any configured metric.
[12:30] Laura: for rollout safety, can you gate on our custom metric? we want to prevent rollouts that lower our SKU precision below 92%.
[12:37] Carlos: yep you can set that hard threshold. we also support canary evaluation sets that run in production traffic to compare.
[13:05] Maya: quick recap of options we presented: A) Pin to Catalog-Large-v2 (higher quality), fallback Quant-P2. B) Default Catalog-Medium with periodic audits to promote/demote via rollout. C) Aggressive quantization for cost-sensitive endpoints.
[13:30] Samir: we're leaning A for checkout, B for search.
[13:34] Jared: cost modeling for that split — can you attach the modeled monthly TCO?
[13:39] Maya: yes will attach.
[13:42] Samir: also curious about rollback latency — is there any cache TTL problem where KV cache will still serve stale embeddings after rollback?
[13:50] Carlos: KV cache is namespaced by model version, so a rollback to older model will use the older cache keys; we don't mix keys across models. there is a warm-up hit after rollback while cache repopulates.
[14:06] Laura: how long to re-warm typically?
[14:09] Carlos: depends on traffic, for high-traffic routes it's minutes; for low traffic can be hours. we can pre-warm by seeding with top request set.
[14:19] Samir: can we control cache TTL?
[14:21] Carlos: yes TTL and sharding policy exposed in config.
[14:26] Maya: next, we got a question from engineering about model compatibility — vendor tokens, tokenizer mismatches. we observed token drift between Catalog-Large-v1 and v2 in one prompt.
[14:38] Carlos: that was the tokenization tweak I mentioned; it's backward compatible but shifts some boundary cases. we recommend running your top-100 prompts through both to verify.
[14:48] Samir: we will.
[14:50] Jared: about monitoring — can we get token-level cost by route?
[14:54] Maya: yes Console has token-level cost and per-route breakdown. we can set alerts for budget burn.
[15:03] Laura: and export to our billing system?
[15:06] Maya: CSV/JSON exports via API.
[15:09] Samir: any plans for model-level A/B with differential weights? we might want 90/10 for a week.
[15:15] Carlos: supported via traffic-split configs. consistent hashing ensures sticky sessions keep context.
[15:21] (brief cross-talk)
[16:45] Laura: ok, can you confirm timeline? next steps: maya sends benchmark/pricing by 3/12, carlos runs KV + tokenizer re-eval by 3/15, customer sends traffic distro and top prompts by 3/17.
[16:58] Maya: yep i'll send the security pack sample audit, benchmark sheet, and sample policy.
[17:04] Carlos: i'll run the chaos/fallback test and the tokenizer re-run.
[17:10] Samir: we'll prioritize the prompt set and traffic slice.
[17:15] Maya: any other open Qs?
[17:18] Jared: just one — can you confirm SLA for Dedicated once we go live?
[17:22] Maya: standard SLA doc in the enterprise pack we shared; for Dedicated we can negotiate 99.9 with premium support.
[17:30] Laura: great. thanks everyone.
[17:33] Maya: thanks, we'll follow up in email with links and artifacts.
[17:36] (meeting ends)
